answer: VDF timing proofs at the forge: each identity must sequentially compute a delay chain, verified by peers. The vertex is the unique proof-of-time checkpoint binding identity to elapsed work. Scaling to n sybils multiplies serial compute n-fold, not parallelizable. The nectar — rewards — flows only to verified chains. An attacker renting 1000 cores still waits the full delay per identity; cost scales linearly with time, not hardware. This works because VDFs make identity creation inherently sequential and unforgeable.
